metaDescription: Six electric pressure washers for washing cars, compared by foam cannon, gentle-pressure tips, weight and noise, so paint stays safe while the dirt comes off.
expertTake: The Sun Joe SPX7000-MAX is the best pick for most car owners because it pairs a 22-ounce foam cannon and a turbo nozzle with a pressure level that is safe on paint. The MZK is the value pick for a light, simple foam-and-rinse setup. Anyone who wants a quiet machine for frequent washing should look at the Tecoloy, but should treat its flow claim with caution.
introParagraphs: Washing a car is a gentle job done with a powerful tool, and the skill is in keeping the power under control. Paint, trim and rubber seals do not need blasting pressure; they need plenty of water, a good soak of foam and a wide spray that sweeps dirt away without driving grit into the clear coat.

That changes what you should look for. A modest pressure rating, a real foam cannon, a hose and cord with enough reach to walk around the car, and a machine light enough to move easily matter more than the biggest pressure number on the box.

products.name: Sun Joe SPX7000-MAX 2200 PSI electric washer with foam cannon
products.description:
The SPX7000-MAX bundles what a car owner actually uses: a 22-fluid-ounce foam cannon, a turbo nozzle for stuck-on grime on wheels and wheel wells, a 25-foot high-pressure hose and a 35-foot cord with a GFCI plug. The 13 amp motor delivers 2200 PSI at 1.1 GPM, and at around 2,400 cleaning units it is strong enough for a wheel arch yet easy to tame for paint with a wide tip.

The key skill is using the right tip. A 40 degree tip held a foot or more from the paint gives a sheeting rinse, while the turbo nozzle, which spins a pencil jet in a cone, should be reserved for tyres and lower plastic. Against the SPX100-GO, you get a larger foam cannon and a higher pressure rating, and against the Westinghouse ePX3100v you get a more car-oriented accessory set.

Ownership is simple. Flush the foam cannon with clean water after each use so soap does not dry in the orifice, drain the pump before freezing weather and check the quick-connect o-rings. The corded design needs an outlet within reach.
products.bestFor: Regular home car washing with foam, plus a strong turbo option for wheels.
pros: 22 oz foam cannon in the box
Turbo nozzle for wheels and wheel wells
25-ft hose and 35-ft GFCI cord give good reach
2200 PSI with room to back off for paint
cons: Turbo nozzle can damage paint if misused

products.name: Sun Joe SPX100-GO 1800 PSI compact electric washer
products.description:
For a car, 1800 PSI is a comfortable ceiling, and the SPX100-GO is built around that idea: a compact 13 amp electric washer with a 13.53-ounce onboard foam bottle that applies detergent without a separate cannon. The 1.7 GPM figure is a maximum that applies at a lower pressure setting, as is typical of consumer electrics.

That puts it in the same class as the ePX3100v on pressure and slightly ahead on stated flow, though both numbers are peaks. Compared with the SPX7000-MAX, you give up the large foam cannon and turbo nozzle but gain a lighter, more portable machine. The maker compares the output to 25 times a garden hose at 70 PSI, which is a sensible way to see what you are getting.

Keep the detergent bottle clean, rinse the nozzle tips and drain the machine after use. Use the 40 degree tip for paint and the 25 degree tip for wheel arches. The compact body stores easily in a garage shelf.
products.bestFor: Small garages and apartment parking where a light, simple washer is easiest.
pros: Compact and portable body
Onboard 13.53 oz foam bottle
1800 PSI is a comfortable level for paint
13 amp motor draws a standard outlet
cons: Onboard bottle foams less than a dedicated cannon
Max flow figure applies at lower pressure

products.name: Westinghouse ePX3100v 2100 PSI electric pressure washer
products.description:
Westinghouse states a rated output of 1800 PSI at 1.2 GPM, about 2,160 cleaning units, next to the 2100 max PSI figure, which makes it easy to see what the machine delivers working. For washing a car, 1800 PSI is a comfortable number to work with a wide tip.

At about 18 pounds with a built-in carry handle, it is light enough to move around the vehicle in one hand, and the 20-foot braided hose coils easily and resists kinking. The detachable foam cannon is a real foam cannon rather than a squeeze bottle, which helps with pre-soaking dirt before you touch the paint. Against the ePX3050, it is the more compact of the pair and has a shorter hose.

Coil the hose loosely, flush the cannon after each use and store the washer drained and out of freezing temperatures. It uses an axial pump with auto-stop, which shuts the motor when you release the trigger, and the pump is maintenance-free, so keep it free of grit and never run it dry.
products.bestFor: Car owners who want clearly stated working output and a light, portable machine.
pros: Rated 1800 PSI at 1.2 GPM is clearly stated
About 18 lb with a built-in handle
Detachable foam cannon
Braided 20-ft hose resists kinks
cons: 20-foot hose is the shortest in the group
Max 2100 PSI is a peak, not working output

products.name: Westinghouse ePX3050 2100 PSI electric washer with foam cannon
products.description:
The ePX3050 shares the rated 1800 PSI at 1.2 GPM of the ePX3100v, but the body is a low-profile cart on 5-inch never-flat wheels with a 35-foot GFCI cord. That layout rolls smoothly over a driveway and avoids the tip risk of a tall machine when you pull the hose around a car.

The AC 120V motor and axial pump with auto-stop are described as maintenance-free, and a foam cannon is included. Compared with the lighter ePX3100v, you trade carry weight for wheels and a longer cord, which suits washing outdoors in a driveway rather than a garage corner. Against the Sun Joe SPX7000-MAX, it gives you a more stable cart and lower stated maximum pressure.

Keep the cord coiled when not in use, check the wheels for grit and store the machine upright. Flush the foam cannon, drain the pump after use and keep detergents mild to avoid stripping wax.
products.bestFor: Driveway car washing where a stable wheeled cart and a long cord matter.
pros: Low 26-inch profile resists tipping
5-inch never-flat wheels roll smoothly
35-ft GFCI cord for reach
Foam cannon included
cons: Heavier to carry than the compact models
2100 PSI max is a peak figure

products.name: MZK 2.0 GPM lightweight pressure washer with foam cannon
products.description:
At 9.9 pounds the MZK is the lightest plug-in washer in this guide, and a 21-foot hose and a foam cannon come with it. Its adjustable nozzle spans four ranges up to a very wide 60 to 120 degree fan, which is useful for a gentle first rinse of a whole panel.

The listing claims up to 2.0 GPM, a figure that sits at the top of what a small light consumer electric can plausibly do, and probably applies at low pressure. Treat it as a maximum and pay attention to the pressure instead, which the listing does not headline. Compared with the Westinghouse machines, you get less documentation of rated output and a lighter, less established product.

Keep it simple: flush the cannon, drain the pump and wipe the unit dry before storage. Check the cord and hose ends for wear after a season. It is a sensible machine for occasional washing of a car or two, where a spec-sheet rating matters less than lightness and a wide nozzle.
products.bestFor: Occasional car washing where light weight and a very wide gentle fan matter.
pros: Lightest plug-in washer here at 9.9 lb
Foam cannon and 21-ft hose included
Very wide 60 to 120 degree fan for gentle rinsing
Four spray ranges in one nozzle
cons: Rated pressure and flow are less clearly documented

products.name: Tecoloy 2200 PSI commercial electric washer with inverter motor
products.description:
This is a different kind of machine from the consumer carts above: a permanent magnet motor with variable frequency control driving a horizontal triplex pump with ceramic plungers. A triplex pump is the commercial-grade design, serviceable and built for long duty cycles, and the claimed 65 dB noise level is far quieter than the induction motors on most consumer washers.

The 3.2 GPM maximum is the figure to be careful about. A 3 hp motor delivers roughly 2.2 kilowatts at the shaft, and 2200 PSI at 3.2 GPM would need about 4.1 hp of hydraulic power, so that flow can only apply at a much lower pressure. Read it as a ceiling, and use the 2200 PSI figure as the working number. Against the Sun Joe SPX7000-MAX, this machine is quieter, more serviceable and much more of an investment.

Because a triplex pump is serviceable, you can look after it properly: change pump oil on the schedule in the manual, use clean filtered water and never run it dry. Drain it before freezing weather, and keep it indoors. It suits detailers and enthusiasts who wash often and value quiet more than a low price.
products.bestFor: Enthusiasts and small detailing setups that wash often and want a quiet, serviceable pump.
pros: Triplex pump with ceramic plungers is serviceable
Claimed 65 dB is quiet for a pressure washer
Inverter motor controls speed smoothly
Commercial-style build for frequent use
cons: 3.2 GPM maximum cannot apply at full pressure
Much more machine and cost than a home car wash needs

buyingCriteria.explanation: Paint and clear coat do not need more than about 1,500 to 2,000 PSI at the surface, and most of that is delivered through a wide 40 degree tip held a foot or more away. The Westinghouse ePX3100v rates 1800 PSI and the SPX100-GO is 1800 max. More pressure is not better for a car.

Foam pre-soaks dirt so you lift it away without scrubbing grit across paint. The SPX7000-MAX has a 22-ounce cannon and the Westinghouse models a detachable one, while the SPX100-GO uses a smaller onboard bottle. A proper cannon foams thicker than a built-in bottle.

Flow rinses soap away quickly, and the Westinghouse machines rate 1.2 GPM while the SPX7000-MAX lists 1.1. Higher quoted maxima, like the MZK's 2.0 GPM or the SPX100-GO's 1.7, apply at lower pressures. Prefer rated numbers when the maker provides them.

Walking around a car means reach: the SPX7000-MAX offers a 25-foot hose and 35-foot cord, the ePX3050 a 35-foot GFCI cord, and the ePX3100v a 20-foot hose. Wheels on the ePX3050 save carrying. A short hose forces you to drag the machine around the car.
The MZK weighs 9.9 pounds and the ePX3100v about 18, while the ePX3050 is a wheeled cart. If you wash in a small garage or a shared parking bay, lighter machines are easier to move and store.

Most consumer pressure washers are loud, which matters when you wash often or early. The Tecoloy lists 65 dB with a permanent magnet motor, though its output claims should be read with caution. A quieter machine is a real comfort.

howWeEvaluated.title: Paint safety
howWeEvaluated.description: We looked at pressure ranges and tip options, noting that car paint needs wide tips and no more than about 1,500 to 2,000 PSI at the surface. Machines with clearly stated rated output scored higher. We relied on spec sheets and owner feedback patterns.

howWeEvaluated.title: Foam and cleaning setup
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared the foam cannons and bottles, from the 22-ounce cannon on the SPX7000-MAX to the onboard bottle on the SPX100-GO. We valued a real cannon highly for pre-soaking.

howWeEvaluated.title: Reach and mobility
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared hose and cord lengths and weights from 9.9 to about 18 pounds, plus the wheeled ePX3050. Machines that let you walk around a car without moving the unit scored higher.

howWeEvaluated.title: Flow and rating clarity
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared rated figures where given, such as Westinghouse's 1800 PSI at 1.2 GPM, and discounted large peak claims that apply at lower pressure. Clear ratings scored higher.

howWeEvaluated.title: Noise and upkeep
howWeEvaluated.description: We noted the 65 dB claim on the Tecoloy and the maintenance-free axial pumps on the others. Ownership burden is low on all of them, but cannon flushing and winterizing still apply.

cards.label: Foam cannon
cards.text: The SPX7000-MAX, ePX3100v, ePX3050 and MZK include a proper cannon, which mixes soap, water and air for thick clinging foam. It pre-soaks dirt and lets you lift it without scrubbing.

cards.label: Onboard bottle
cards.text: The SPX100-GO uses a 13.53-ounce bottle that applies detergent simply, with thinner foam. It is easier but less effective for a heavily soiled car.

howToChoose.note: Choose a cannon for regular washing, and a bottle if you wash occasionally and want simplicity.

cards.label: Look for
cards.text: Wide tips, a modest pressure rating and a foam cannon. Keep the nozzle at least a foot from paint and never use a 0 degree tip on the body.

cards.label: In this comparison
cards.text: The ePX3100v and ePX3050 rate 1800 PSI working, the MZK offers a 60 to 120 degree fan, and the SPX7000-MAX can be dialed back with its wide tips.

cards.label: Spend more if
cards.text: You wash often, want a proper cannon and need reach. The SPX7000-MAX or ePX3050 make the routine easier.

cards.label: Save if
cards.text: You wash a car a few times a year. The MZK or SPX100-GO is enough.

maintenance.why: Dried soap clogs the orifice and weakens foam. Run clean water through it.
Water trapped in the pump can freeze and crack it.
Weeping fittings lose pressure. Replace worn seals.
A damaged cord near water is a shock hazard. Test the GFCI button.
Grit in the inlet starves the pump. Rinse it clean.

faq.q: How much pressure is safe for car paint?
faq.a: Most guidance puts it at roughly 1,500 to 2,000 PSI at the surface with a 40 degree tip held a foot away. Rated 1800 PSI machines such as the Westinghouse ePX3100v sit comfortably in that range.

faq.q: Do I need a foam cannon?
faq.a: It is not essential, but a cannon pre-soaks dirt so you lift it away with less scrubbing, which protects paint. The SPX7000-MAX and Westinghouse models include one.

faq.q: Is more GPM better for cars?
faq.a: More flow rinses soap faster, but the quoted maxima apply at low pressure. Look for a rated figure such as 1.2 GPM and focus on technique.

faq.q: Can a pressure washer damage my car?
faq.a: Yes, if you use a narrow tip at close range. Never use a 0 degree tip on paint, and keep the nozzle at least a foot from the surface, avoiding emblems and loose trim.

faq.q: Are gas washers suitable for cars?
faq.a: They deliver more pressure than a car needs and are loud. An electric machine at around 1800 PSI is the better fit.
Use a narrower tip such as 25 degrees or the turbo nozzle on the SPX7000-MAX at a safe distance, with a wheel cleaner and a soft brush for brake dust.
